chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who has a right against another man, and the debtor denies it and swears that he has no right against him, and the creditor has no clear proof for his right; is it permissible for us to revive his right through false testimony if he fears [loss]? He said: 'It is not permissible due to the reason of tidlis (concealment/deception).'

key_terms.التَّدْلِيسُ: Concealment, subtle deception, or feigning knowledge
key_terms.الزُّورُ: Falsehood or perjury; here referring to false testimony

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to use false witnesses to prove a debt if the debtor denies it and swears an oath?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that using false testimony to establish a debt is impermissible due to *al-tadlis* (subtle deception or concealment of truth), distinguishing it from straightforward falsehood. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the integrity of evidence, where the method of establishing a right must be as truthful as the right itself, preventing the corruption of legal proceedings through strategic deceit.
